neighbours.label: Broad pole; best guess: nouns for organised human arrangements in institutional prose (program, members, project, method, strategies, system, relationships), versus concrete physical scenes
fire: Since the launch of the program, attendance at the evening classes has doubled.
Only paid-up members can vote at the annual meeting of the club.
Each project has a budget, a timetable and a named manager.
The course teaches study strategies such as summarising, self-testing and spacing.
Researchers compared the two methods and found that the newer one was faster.
The mentoring program pairs new members with experienced volunteers.
Strong relationships between teachers and parents help the whole system work.
Our system tracks every project from the first proposal to the final report.
quiet: Since the end of the frost, blossom on the apple trees has opened.
Only ripe plums fall from the branches of the tree by the wall.
Each cottage has a chimney, a blue door and a small garden.
The cook chops onions, carrots and celery and drops them in the pot.
Children climbed the two hills and found that the steeper one was muddy.
The grey cat sleeps on the warm stones beside the sleeping dog.
Thick fog between the cliffs and the harbour kept the fishing boats tied up.
Our kettle whistles every morning from the first light to the last cup of tea.
